level_1: Obtains and performs developmentally appropriate history and physical exam
level_2: Selects and interprets diagnostic testing
level_3: Develops a plan to manage patients with straightforward conditions
level_4: Develops a plan to manage patients with complex conditions and adapts plan for changing clinical situation
level_5: Develops a clinical pathway for the management of patients with complex conditions

level_1: Describes how changes in normal physiology may lead to peri- procedural alterations and complications
level_2: Accurately and reliably gathers and reports clinical information pertaining to common peri-procedural alterations and complications
level_3: Identifies and prioritizes tasks necessary for management of peri- procedural alterations and complications
level_4: Proactively recognizes potential risk factors for complications and implements measures to prevent or mitigate them
level_5: Coordinates input from multiple specialties and/or manages multiple scenarios simultaneously

level_1: Prepares pediatric patients and equipment for endoscopic procedures
Selects ureteroscope and stent size for individual patients and plans for assistive devices to perform endoscopic procedures
level_2: Identifies anatomic and safety differences between pediatric and adult populations
Independently performs complex endoscopic procedures
level_3: Independently performs diagnostic pediatric lower tract endoscopic procedures
Selects endoscopic assistive devices in a cost-effective manner and effectively troubleshoots during the procedure
level_4: Identifies urethral and ureteral abnormalities during endoscopic procedures
Independently performs complex endoscopic procedures in a patient with challenging anatomy
level_5: Independently performs simple diagnostic upper tract and lower tract therapeutic endoscopic procedures
Identifies a novel use of available tools

level_1: Describes various published techniques available for open procedures
level_2: Anticipates the steps of the procedure and actively assists
level_3: Performs simple open procedures with good tissue handling and identifies the need for deviation in the surgical plan
level_4: Performs complex open procedures and executes deviation in the surgical plan when needed
level_5: Performs procedures incorporating surgical innovations

level_1: Describes various published techniques available for reconstruction
level_2: Anticipates the steps of the procedure and actively assists
level_3: Performs routine genital procedures with good tissue handling and identifies the need for deviation from the surgical plan
level_4: Performs complex genital procedures and deviates from the surgical plan when needed
level_5: Performs procedures incorporating surgical innovations

level_1: Prepares pediatric patients and equipment for minimally invasive procedures
level_2: Actively assists and performs portions of the minimally invasive procedure
level_3: Performs low complexity minimally invasive procedures with good tissue handling and identifies need for deviation in the surgical plan or conversion to open approach
level_4: Performs complex minimally invasive procedures and deviates from the surgical plan when needed
level_5: Performs procedures incorporating surgical innovations

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of anatomy and physiology of the genitourinary tract as it relates to pediatric patients
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of pathophysiology and treatments of simple conditions, including guidelines
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of pathophysiology and treatments of complex conditions, taking individual patient factors into consideration (e.g., contributing bowel and bladder dysfunction, familial preferences)
level_4: Demonstrates knowledge of the full spectrum of congenital conditions, including rare diseases, controversies, and evolving treatment practices
level_5: Advances understanding of pathophysiology or clinical care pathways in pediatric urology

level_1: Integrates patient- specific information to generate an appropriate working diagnosis
level_2: Provides a prioritized differential diagnosis using supporting rationale
level_3: Independently synthesizes clinical information to inform diagnosis and therapy in simple cases and adapts based on a patient’s clinical course and additional data
level_4: Independently synthesizes clinical information to inform diagnosis and therapy in complex cases, recognizing sources of error
level_5: Teaches others to recognize sources of diagnostic error

level_1: Understands long-term ramifications of urinary tract, renal function, gastrointestinal function, and reproductive health
Lists care requirements for pediatric patients with chronic genitourinary conditions as they age and grow
level_2: Demonstrates basic knowledge of embryology and physiologic changes with aging in the genitourinary system
Actively contributes to the medical and psychological well-being of patients with complex conditions
level_3: Identifies role of other specialists to achieve goals of care
Identifies potential complications and long- term adult needs for patients with chronic genitourinary conditions arising in childhood
level_4: Describes initial treatment options for patients born with genitourinary conditions requiring long- term care
Advocates locally and nationally for psychological well-being and collaborative care of chronic conditions
level_5: Engages with other specialists for comprehensive care
Develops clinical curriculum related to care transition from child to adulthood for chronic genitourinary conditions

level_1: Participates in basic patient safety initiatives (e.g., time-outs, handwashing protocols)
Identifies potential areas for team or local quality improvement initiatives
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
Actively engages care team to prevent patient safety events
level_3: Identifies and reports patient safety events
Demonstrates the skills required to develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_4: Describes and participates in local quality improvement initiatives (e.g., multimodal analgesics, antibiotic stewardship, hospital acquired infection)
Enacts systemic changes to prevent patient safety events by affecting processes
level_5: Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual) and offers strategies to prevent future events
Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community level

level_1: Advocates for quality patient care and identifies potential barriers to care
Supervises safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs of junior team members
level_2: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations
Coordinates multidisciplinary care of patients in complex clinical situations by incorporating local resources into the plan (e.g., social worker to identify additional home resources)
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of local resources available for optimizing care delivery and coordination
Resolves conflicts in transitions of care between teams
level_4: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations
Designs innovative care coordination strategies for optimizing health care outcomes, taking into consideration populations with specific health care needs
level_5: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations, considering potential barriers to care including health needs, language differences, and family circumstances
Leads in the design and implementation of improved transitions of care

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Understands different types of physician practices and the basic differences/benefits and liabilities associated with each (e.g., private practice versus academic, solo practitioner versus group practice)
Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system performance (e.g., length of stay, readmission rates, clinical efficiency)
level_2: Describes basic health payment systems (e.g., government, private, public, uninsured care) and practice models
Describes core administrative knowledge needed for transition to independent practice (e.g., cost/billing effectiveness)
level_3: Demonstrates use of information technology required for medical practice (e.g., electronic health record, documentation required for billing and coding)
Manages various components of the complex health care system to provide efficient and effective patient care (e.g., patient payment models, insurance)
level_4: Describes how components of a complex health care system are interrelated and how this impacts patient care
Analyzes professional requirements in preparation for practice (e.g., contract negotiations, malpractice insurance, government regulation, compliance)
level_5: Identifies basic needs for effective transition to practice (e.g., information technology, legal, billing and coding, financial)
Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient, and effective patient care

level_1: Demonstrates how to access available evidence
level_2: Articulates clinical questions to guide evidence-based care
level_3: Integrates best available evidence with patient preferences to guide care
level_4: Tailors patient care in the setting of conflicting or absent evidence
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence for patients with complex conditions

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Accepts feedback from faculty members
Integrates practice data to revise goals
level_2: Establishes goals for personal and professional development
Seeks out specific feedback to further improve performance
level_3: Uses feedback from all members of the team to improve performance
Uses performance data to measure readiness for independent clinical practice
level_4: Monitors progress towards goals and directs efforts accordingly
Coaches others to integrate feedback and improve performance
level_5: Integrates feedback and adjusts behaviors in real time to improve performance
Coaches others to incorporate performance data

level_1: Demonstrates professional behavior in routine situations and knows how to report professionalism lapses
Seeks help in managing and resolving complex ethical situations
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of ethical principles underlying shared decision making and patient confidentiality
Recognizes and intervenes in situations to prevent professionalism lapses in oneself and others
level_3: Demonstrates insight into personal triggers for professionalism lapses and develops mitigation strategies
Recognizes and uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas (e.g., ethics consultations, literature review)
level_4: Analyzes straightforward situations using ethical principles
Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_5: Demonstrates professional behavior in complex or stressful situations
Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution

level_1: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in routine situations
level_2: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex and stressful situations
level_3: Delegates and oversees tasks to medical students and residents that results in efficient management of clinical activities and enhances education
level_4: Recognizes situations that may impact others’ ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner and proposes solutions
level_5: Develops systems to enhance others’ ability to efficiently complete administrative tasks and responsibilities

level_1: With assistance, recognizes status of personal and professional well-being
level_2: Independently recognizes status of personal and professional well-being
level_3: Identifies how well-being impacts the team’s performance
level_4: Independently develops a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being
level_5: Coaches others when emotional responses do not meet professional expectations

level_1: Demonstrates respect and establishes rapport with patients and patients’ families (e.g., situational awareness of language, disability, health literacy level)
When prompted, reflects on biases while attempting to minimize communication barriers
level_2: Communicates with patients and their families in an understandable and respectful manner
Facilitates difficult discussions specific to patient and family conferences, (e.g., end- of-life, explaining complications, therapeutic uncertainty)
level_3: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in straightforward encounters
Independently recognizes biases while attempting to proactively minimize communication barriers
level_4: Identifies barriers to effective communication (e.g., health literacy)
Mentors others in situational awareness and critical self-reflection
level_5: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in challenging encounters (e.g., shared decision making)
Coaches others in the facilitation of crucial conversations

subcompetencies.name: Patient Counseling and Shared Decision Making

level_1: Demonstrates basic understanding of the informed consent process
level_2: Answers questions from patients and caregivers about treatment plans and seeks guidance when appropriate
level_3: Counsels patients and caregivers through decision-making process using developmentally appropriate language for simple clinical and surgical problems
level_4: Counsels patients and caregivers through decision-making process using developmentally appropriate language for complex clinical and surgical problems
level_5: Leads patients, caregivers, and team in complex and high-risk decision making and counseling

level_1: Respectfully interacts and actively communicates with all members of health care team (e.g., proper identification, politely accepts and requests consults)
level_2: Communicates in an approachable and productive manner to facilitate teamwork (e.g., active listening, updates in timely fashion)
level_3: Actively recognizes and mitigates communication barriers and biases with members of the health care team
level_4: Identifies conflict as threat to patient care and team functioning and initiates an intervention
level_5: Exemplifies flexible communication strategies

level_1: Accurately records information in the patient record in a timely manner while safeguarding patient personal health information
level_2: Documents diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning in the patient record with appropriate use of documentation shortcuts
level_3: Concisely reports diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning
level_4: Efficiently communicates in an organized fashion that includes contingency plans
level_5: Facilitates improved written and verbal communication of others
